title: The remaining power is free from coercion and physical necessity; many call it a physical power to do good
source_text: XLVIII. Praeterea eosdem fateri potentiam istam in homine post peccatum residuam, respectu eorundem operum liberam esse, non tantum a coactione, sed etiam ab omni Physica necessitate, & determinatione bruta. Unde est quod eorum multi dicere non verentur, hominem ante gratiam potentiam Physicam habere salutare bonum operandi, illumque posse bene operari si velit, licet ad hoc sit moraliter impotens, propter voluntatem ejus pravis habitibus in malo obfirmatam.
pass_a_gloss: XLVIII. Moreover that the same confess that that power remaining in man after sin is free in respect of the same works, not only from coaction, but also from every Physical necessity, and brute determination. Whence it is that many of them are not afraid to say, that man before grace has the Physical power of working saving good, and that he can work well if he will, although for this he is morally unable, on account of his will hardened in evil by depraved habits.
pass_b_english: They also grant that the power left in man after sin is free with respect to those works, not only from compulsion but from all physical necessity and brute determination.

That is why many of them do not hesitate to say that man before grace has a physical power to do saving good and can do good if he wills, though he is morally unable to do it because his will is hardened in evil by perverse habits.

lemmas.latin: non tantum a coactione, sed etiam ab omni Physica necessitate
lemmas.gloss: not only from coaction, but also from every Physical necessity
hardened in evil by depraved habits

choices.why: Inability that lies in the will's settled disposition, opposed to physical inability (lack of the faculty or outside hindrance); kept as the technical pair.
